patient_information: A 4-year-old girl in good general health.
chief_complaint: A slowly growing, moderately painful nodule on the fifth toe of her right foot.
history_of_present_illness: The nodule developed over several days and caused pain when wearing shoes; her 9-year-old brother has similar lesions on two toes.
exposure_and_epidemiology: The family moved from Chile to the Cochabamba region in Bolivia about 6 months ago, where they live on a farm.
physical_exam: Close to the root of the fifth toenail of the right foot there is a dark-brown small nodule with a tiny central ulceration, surrounded by minimal inflammatory reaction; white oval granules were observed emerging from the nodule when parents tried to squeeze it.
labs_and_diagnostics: Microscopic examination of removed tissue showed parts of a female flea (arrow) and typical eggs.
management_and_clinical_course: The parasite was completely removed using a sterile needle and/or curette, followed by disinfection and dressing of the resulting round lesion; the skin lesion healed within a week without complications.
